description: Create a user-created (custom) IAM policy with explicit permission statements — the way to scope a sub account to specific actions and resources instead of using a broad system-managed policy. Max 500 policies per account. Use ncloud_validate_policy first for real server-side validation; dryRun=true only echoes the request shape.

dryRun.description: If true, returns a preview without actually creating the policy

permissions.description: Permission statements. Each entry allows a set of actions on a set of resource NRNs for one service

condition.description: Optional policy condition, shaped as {operator: {conditionKey: [values]}}. Example: {"StringEquals": {"ncp:RequestRegion": ["KR"]}}

effect.description: Whether the permission is allowed. "Allow" is the only valid value

targets.description: Permission targets: which service, actions and resources this permission covers

actions.description: Allowed actions. Use an exact action name for fine-grained control, "View*" for all read actions, "Change*" for all mutating actions, or "*" for the whole service

product.description: Service code of the target service (e.g. Server, DataQuery, ObjectStorage). See the Ncloud per-service permission reference for valid codes

resourceNrns.description: Target resource NRNs (e.g. "nrn:PUB:DataQuery:KR:123456:DataSource/2942"). Use ["*"] for every resource of the product — note the server rewrites that into a product-scoped NRN (["*"] on product Server comes back as ["nrn:*:Server:*::*"]), so a read-back through ncloud_get_policy_detail will not equal the string you sent

policyName.description: Policy name (3-30 chars: Korean/Japanese/English letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'; must start with a letter)

tags.description: Tags as a key-value map, max 20 per resource. Example: {"env":"dev","team":"a"}

name: ncloud_create_policy
